commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36687: test: wait for the node to finish the last block in p2p_ping_ibd

9af82f9872ca1a9e8d4645c537b23af4bc861ed2 test: wait for the node to finish the last block in p2p_ping_ibd (Greg Sanders)

Pull request description:

  ProcessBlock() stamps m_last_block_time only after ProcessNewBlock() returns, so getblockcount can show the new height, with nothing in flight, before the stamp is taken. A bumpmocktime in that gap stamps the block with the bumped time, and the final bump then leaves the ping timeout exactly at its boundary, where it never fires. Sync with a ping after the last block, so the node has finished processing it before the clock moves.

  The race has been present since the test was added in #36080.

  Faling job:
  https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/actions/runs/40589303246/job/122489039018

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#35818: bloom: avoid undefined sizing calculations

c4302ddf806094fcc2b1e21593e25b2038191a07 fuzz: cover bloom sizing boundaries (Lőrinc)
3acd9ae9016e6c66783bec002435a49c04050db2 test: cover bloom sizing boundaries (Lőrinc)
77055771169dc44f832083f46468ea75421a009b bloom: avoid undefined sizing calculations (Lőrinc)
3614b38e33cb98528b0c3dc337060f7448bb8e6e test: characterize bloom filter sizing (Lőrinc)

Pull request description:

  **Problem:** The four-argument `CBloomFilter` constructor is used by unit tests and the fuzz target to exercise Bloom filter sizing directly.
  Zero elements make the hash-function calculation divide by zero.
  The size calculation converts its floating-point result to `unsigned int` before applying the protocol limit, which is undefined for zero or invalid false-positive rates and for valid parameters whose calculated size exceeds the integer range.

  **Fix:** Require false-positive rates in `[0, 1]`, construct the existing empty match-all state for zero elements, and use the largest permitted filter for a zero rate with positive elements.
  Clamp the calculated size before its integer conversion so large valid inputs remain within the protocol limit.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36011: btcsignals: destroy callbacks on disconnect

a318b23131e6df2c64e8fe79cebc8e5babdf8b7f btcsignals: fall back to atomic_load/store without __cpp_lib_atomic_shared_ptr (Ryan Ofsky)
f1d786c1ef5d813f61e405370a67df4cc6323885 btcsignals: destroy callbacks eagerly on disconnect (Ryan Ofsky)
7c5571adc46857cfcf77d81b6fc135dee5369749 test: characterize btcsignals callback destruction timing (Ryan Ofsky)

Pull request description:

  Currently callback functions connected to signals do not get freed when their `connection::disconnect` method is called or when their associated `scoped_connection` is destroyed. They live as long as the signal does, even if they will never be called, and can only get [garbage collected](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/blob/0fd515bbb7070a502dd2fe6d16f5f3cbac591283/src/util/btcsignals.h#L240-L241) if new connections are added.

  This behavior is different that previous boost signals behavior and causes a [deadlock](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/actions/runs/31848571315/job/94919834743) on GUI shutdown in #10102 because when the node registers signal callbacks (`handleInitMessage`, etc) that get forwarded to the GUI, the callbacks own `mp::EventLoopRef` references, and if the callbacks aren't freed, the node process can't shut down.

  This change restores boost signals behavior freeing callbacks when they are disconnected or when `scoped_connection` objects are destroyed to avoid this problem and make callback lifetimes more predictable.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36594: net: make orphan reconsideration more granular

83003cafaa81bb116526419246608658ede824b6 qa: test a single orphan is processed per peer turn, regardless of its validation result (Antoine Poinsot)
28a41e61ab5d993d344dc5c8180482eb146c6bd5 net: reconsider at most one orphan per call, whatever the validation result (Antoine Poinsot)

Pull request description:

  We currently concentrate the validation of all the assigned peer’s reconsiderable orphans that are still missing inputs in a single message-processing turn. This ties orphan processing to validation result, and adds latency to processing other peers' messages.

  `HTTPRemoteClient::TryReadRequest()` only needs to be a `static` method in order to forward a `shared_ptr` of a client to a new request.

  ### Commits solving these issues in same order

  * http: Remove `HTTPRequest::SetState()` and introduce `HTTPRequest::Load()` - Removes the ability for other classes to directly modify the request state.
  * 2 refactors: Extract `HTTPRemoteClient::TryReadRequestInternal()` from a combination of `HTTPRemoteClient::TryReadRequest()` and `HTTPRemoteClient::ReadRequest()` (the latter is removed)

Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36606: test, bench: construct inputs/outputs declaratively in context-dependent cases

bdf58dd89cc2fe2f0be5ac63755e821661022be6 test: construct transaction_tests test_Get inputs/outputs declaratively (Alexander Wiederin)
24d00c4539479415207d3b912ec3648b4020c4e0 bench: construct ccoins_caching inputs/outputs declaratively (Alexander Wiederin)
a45478aa27553d28479cb288bb2d33f917bc544b test: construct sigopcount_tests BuildTxs inputs/outputs declaratively (Alexander Wiederin)
524d554e2bf952082f7e621145ca1b3a4b81d6c7 test: construct CreateBlockChain coinbase declaratively (Alexander Wiederin)
60be0930ca92eeee960ef6a2d7e2c61ef03c93dd test: construct transaction_utils inputs/outputs declaratively (Alexander Wiederin)

Pull request description:

  Part of https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/36692 (previously discussed in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35994): replace procedural, field-by-field construction of `COutPoint`, `CTxIn` and `CTxOut` in test code with constructor calls.

  This PR covers cases that are context-dependent and need manual changes, independent of a scripted-diff for the trivial bulk:
  - `test/util/transaction_utils`: in `BuildSpendingTransaction`, the `scriptWitness` assignment has to be moved after `vin` is replaced, otherwise the witness is dropped.
  - `test/util/mining`: in `CreateBlockChain`, the coinbase input's fields were split by the output assignments, with comments that are now kept next to the constructor arguments.
  - `sigopcount_tests`: `BuildTxs` has the same witness ordering issue as `BuildSpendingTransaction`.
  - `bench/ccoins_caching`: The `scriptSig`s are built with `<<` appends, and the second output was created by `vout.resize(2)` but never assigned, so it is kept as a null `CTxOut{}`.
  - `transaction_tests`: `test_Get` builds the same transaction as `bench/ccoins_caching`, with the same `<<` appends and null second output.

  **This change is test- and bench-only and does not change the constructed transactions.**

  Notes for reviewers:
  - `CTxIn` has no witness constructor argument, so `scriptWitness` is assigned after `vin` is replaced.
  - `BuildTxs` is called repeatedly on the same transaction objects. Previously, `resize(1)` kept the existing inputs and only overwrote some of their fields; now they are replaced entirely. The fields that were left untouched by `BuildTxs` are never modified by the test, so the transactions are unchanged.
  - The null second output in `ccoins_caching` is copied from `test_Get` in `transaction_tests` and looks like an oversight. It is kept here to avoid behaviour changes.

commit.message:
Merge bitcoin/bitcoin#36682: refactor: Use std::erase and std::erase_if

fa87bfe31dfda2d102c4e0cb5d39813cf84c7d1e refactor: Use std::erase and std::erase_if over iterator-based erase (MarcoFalke)
fa93a02563145aca3f96badaabe302b2dfa331d5 refactor: Use std::erase and std::erase_if over list removal or vector erase-remove (MarcoFalke)

Pull request description:

  Convert `remove` and `remove_if` to the C++20 `std::erase` and `std::erase_if` overloads.

  The legacy ones can be confusing, because:

  * Array-based containers (like vector) must use the erase-remove idiom. Forgetting the erase, or forgetting to pass the end iterator (`bugprone-inaccurate-erase`) can be a bug, see also https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36588#discussion_r4345799022. So a call only to "remove" will not erase.
  * Node-based containers (like list or set) must not use the idiom. Using it will be a pessimization or won't compile. And correctly not using the idiom reads confusing, because a call to "remove" will actually erase.
  * They are more verbose.

  Also convert simple iterator-erase (which is verbose, but fine) to the std overload.
